articles.title: KURA Announces Three-Hour Outer Ring Road Closure This Saturday
articles.desc: Nairobi motorists will face disruption on Outer Ring Road this Saturday as KURA removes an overhead gantry near Airport North Road.
articles.content:
Nairobi motorists using Outer Ring Road have been advised to plan their journeys ahead of a scheduled three-hour traffic disruption this Saturday, September 5, 2026.

The Kenya Urban Roads Authority (KURA) announced on Wednesday, September 2, that part of the busy Nairobi road will be affected between 12pm and 3pm to allow for the removal of an overhead gantry near the Airport North Road junction.

According to the traffic management plan, the operation will take place in three stages. From 12pm to 1pm, machinery will be moved into position while traffic continues at reduced speed.

The affected section will then face a full closure between 1pm and 2pm as crews remove the gantry. Traffic is expected to resume from 2pm to 3pm, although motorists may still experience reduced speeds as equipment is removed and the work area is cleared.

KURA has urged motorists to plan their travel in advance and cooperate with traffic police officers and marshals who will be deployed during the operation.

The Nairobi Outer Ring Road closure is likely to affect motorists travelling through the eastern parts of the city, particularly those connecting through the Airport North Road area.

Outer Ring Road is an important transport corridor linking major routes and serving thousands of commuters and public service vehicles daily. Any temporary closure along the route can therefore cause delays, especially during busy weekend travel periods.

Motorists travelling through the area may need to consider alternative routes depending on their destination. Routes around Mombasa Road, Airport South Road and Airport North Road have been identified in traffic advisories as options for avoiding the affected section.

For Nairobi residents, the latest KURA traffic advisory is important because the disruption has been announced several days before the planned works, giving motorists, matatu operators and businesses time to adjust their travel plans.

Drivers planning to use Outer Ring Road on Saturday afternoon are advised to allow extra travel time, avoid the affected section during the full closure where possible and follow instructions issued by traffic officers at the site.

The works are scheduled to end at 3pm on Saturday, after which normal traffic flow is expected to resume.

articles.title: Court Told Key Nairobi CCTV Cameras Were Offline During Rex Masai Shooting
articles.desc: An inquest has heard that key Nairobi CBD CCTV cameras were offline during the 2024 shooting of protester Rex Masai.
articles.content:
Key police CCTV cameras in Nairobi's Central Business District were offline when protester Rex Masai was fatally shot during the June 2024 anti-Finance Bill demonstrations, a court has heard.

The fresh details emerged on Tuesday during the ongoing inquest into Masai's death, where Chief Inspector Andrew Limo, a technical officer attached to the National Police Service CCTV command centre, testified about the state of the surveillance network.

Limo told the court that cameras detectives wanted to rely on for footage were not operational at the time of the shooting.

Among them was a camera along Mama Ngina Street, an area linked to the events surrounding the demonstrations in Nairobi's CBD.

The court heard that a faulty fibre cable had affected parts of the CCTV network, leaving investigators without some of the recordings they had sought after the shooting.

The testimony has raised fresh questions about the reliability of surveillance systems in one of Nairobi's busiest areas.

CCTV footage can play an important role in investigations by helping authorities reconstruct events, identify people and establish timelines.

However, Limo told the court that the relevant cameras were offline when investigators sought footage connected to the June 20, 2024 demonstrations.

He was also questioned about whether the cameras around Mama Ngina Street had since been restored.

According to his testimony, the cameras remained offline.

The issue is significant for Nairobi because the CBD is a major centre for business, transport and public activity, where surveillance infrastructure can play an important role in security and investigations.

During the hearing, questions were raised about how investigators would handle a serious incident in an area where surveillance cameras were unavailable.

Limo told the court that police investigations do not rely entirely on CCTV footage and can use other sources of evidence.

The testimony does not determine responsibility for Masai's death, which remains the subject of the ongoing inquest. Instead, it adds fresh information about the availability of surveillance footage during the demonstrations.

The hearing was adjourned and is expected to continue as the court examines further evidence connected to the case.

For Nairobi residents, the latest testimony also brings renewed attention to the condition and maintenance of security infrastructure in the city centre.

articles.title: JKIA Flights Resume After Aviation Workers Call Off Strike
articles.desc: JKIA operations are resuming after aviation workers called off their strike, with efforts underway to clear disrupted flights.
articles.content:
Flight operations at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport are beginning to return to normal after aviation workers called off a strike that disrupted travel and left passengers facing delays and cancellations.

The Kenya Aviation Workers Union ended the industrial action on Tuesday following talks with the government and aviation authorities.

Under a return-to-work agreement, affected workers were directed to resume their normal duties as efforts began to restore services and clear flights affected during the disruption.

The strike had caused significant problems at JKIA, Kenya's main international airport, with passengers experiencing long delays, cancellations and uncertainty over their travel plans.

For many travellers, the announcement that workers had returned to duty brings relief, but normal operations may take time to fully recover as airlines and airport authorities work through flights disrupted during the strike.

JKIA is one of East Africa's most important aviation hubs, meaning disruptions at the airport can affect not only Nairobi travellers but also regional and international connections.

The return to work is therefore expected to ease pressure on passengers, airlines and businesses that depend on reliable air transport.

The latest development follows days of disruption that left some travellers stranded and forced others to change their plans at short notice.

Passengers with upcoming flights are still advised to confirm their travel status directly with their airlines, particularly as schedules are adjusted while operations are restored.

The agreement ending the strike is also important because it shifts attention from the immediate disruption to whether the issues raised by aviation workers will now be addressed through the agreed process.

For Nairobi residents and travellers, the immediate focus remains the restoration of reliable airport services and the clearance of delayed flights.

As workers resume their duties, authorities will be under pressure to restore normal operations as quickly as possible and reduce further inconvenience for passengers.

articles.title: Stolen Phone Leads Police to Suspected Nairobi Handset Network
articles.desc: A stolen phone led police to a Nairobi shop where 12 other handsets were recovered as investigations into a suspected network continue.
articles.content:
A stolen mobile phone has led police to a shop in Nairobi suspected of being linked to the illegal trade in stolen handsets, opening fresh investigations into a possible wider network.

Officers from Embakasi and Central police stations launched an undercover operation along Munyu Road after receiving information about the stolen device.

The operation led to the arrest of a suspect, who police say provided investigators with leads after questioning.

According to the National Police Service, the suspect allegedly said he had bought the phone from people known to him before selling it on.

A search at the premises later uncovered 12 additional mobile phones and six phone batteries, raising suspicion that the location may have been used to receive and trade in stolen devices.

Police are now pursuing other suspects identified during the operation as investigations continue into how the alleged network operates and how stolen phones move through the trade.

The case matters to Nairobi residents because mobile phone theft remains a daily concern in many parts of the city. For victims, losing a phone can mean more than losing an expensive device, particularly where personal information, mobile money services and important contacts are involved.

The latest operation also shifts attention to the market that may exist after a phone is stolen. Recovering suspected devices can help investigators trace possible links between those who steal phones and individuals accused of receiving or reselling them.

The National Police Service has urged members of the public to report suspicious activity to the nearest police station.

As investigations continue, police are expected to establish whether the Munyu Road operation was linked to a broader network dealing in stolen handsets.

For Nairobi residents, the outcome could provide important answers about how stolen phones are moved and sold within the city and whether those behind the alleged trade can be brought to account.

articles.title: Hundreds Remain Stranded at JKIA as Aviation Workers' Strike Continues
articles.desc: Hundreds of passengers remain stranded at JKIA as an aviation workers' strike enters its second day, disrupting flights and airport operations.
articles.content:
Hundreds of passengers remained stranded at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport on Monday as an aviation workers' strike continued to disrupt flights and airport operations.

Some travellers spent Sunday night at the airport after delays and uncertainty affected their travel plans. Others arrived on Monday hoping to board rescheduled flights but were still waiting for updates on when they would depart.

The disruption followed industrial action involving members of the Kenya Aviation Workers Union, whose grievances include concerns over welfare, working conditions and the implementation of previously agreed employment benefits.

The strike has affected aviation operations beyond Nairobi, but JKIA has become the centre of the disruption because of its role as Kenya's main international aviation hub.

For passengers, the impact has gone beyond delayed flights. Travellers have faced uncertainty over connections, accommodation and changes to plans that may have been arranged days or weeks earlier.

Some airlines have reportedly begun making arrangements for affected passengers, including hotel transfers in certain cases, as the disruption continues.

The situation also highlights the wider effect of industrial disputes at critical public facilities. A disruption at JKIA can quickly affect travellers, airlines, businesses and families, particularly when passengers are connecting to regional and international destinations.

Airport authorities have also advised passengers to confirm their flight status with their respective airlines before travelling, as delays continue to affect departures.

The immediate concern for travellers is when normal operations will resume and whether the dispute between workers and the affected aviation institutions can be resolved.

For those still waiting at JKIA, however, the most pressing issue remains clear: receiving reliable information about their flights and knowing when their journeys can continue.

As the strike enters its second day, attention will remain on negotiations and any agreement that could restore normal operations at Kenya's busiest airport.

articles.title: Youth Storm Utimo Sacco Offices Over Death of Man in Matatu Incident
articles.desc: Youth and community members stormed Utimo Sacco offices in Buruburu, demanding accountability over the death of Brian Wafula.
articles.content:
Youth and community members staged protests in Nairobi on Saturday after storming the offices of Utimo Matatu Sacco in Buruburu, demanding accountability over the death of Brian Wafula.

The protests followed an incident reported to have occurred about two weeks ago near Space Mall in Umoja. Wafula allegedly died after being pushed from a moving matatu following a dispute over payment.

According to accounts from his colleagues, Wafula had helped the matatu crew free their vehicle after it became stuck in mud. A disagreement later emerged over payment for the assistance.

Wafula reportedly boarded the vehicle while demanding the money he was owed. During the confrontation, he was allegedly pushed from the moving matatu and suffered serious head injuries.

His death has now triggered anger among colleagues and members of the community, leading to Saturday's protest at the Sacco offices.

Police were deployed as protesters blocked access to the offices and demanded answers over the incident.

The matter remains under investigation. Police in Buruburu said the matatu linked to the incident has been traced and impounded for examination, while efforts to locate the crew involved continue.

The case has drawn attention to accountability in public transport and the safety of passengers and other people who interact with matatus on Nairobi's busy roads.

For Wafula's family and colleagues, however, the immediate concern remains justice and the identification of those responsible for his death.

His body remains at the Mama Lucy Hospital morgue as the family prepares for his burial. Family members and colleagues have also appealed for support to help facilitate the funeral arrangements.

Saturday's protests add fresh pressure for progress in the investigation as the community awaits further action from police.

As investigations continue, the case is expected to remain under close watch, particularly over whether the matatu crew will be traced and held accountable if evidence establishes criminal responsibility.

articles.title: Gikomba Market Takes Shape as Nairobi Redevelopment Moves Forward
articles.desc: Three new multi-storey blocks are taking shape at Gikomba as Nairobi's major market undergoes redevelopment aimed at improving trading and safety.
articles.content:
Gikomba Market is taking a major step toward a new look, with three multi-storey blocks now under construction as the redevelopment of one of Nairobi's busiest trading centres moves forward.

An update issued on Wednesday by Interior Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo said roofing and internal installation works are underway on the three blocks forming the first phase of the project. 

The first phase is expected to provide trading spaces for up to 7,000 traders, including a dedicated fish-processing area designed for about 300 traders. The planned facilities also include a day-care centre, kitchens, sanitation facilities, an ICT hub, youth centre, basement parking, waste collection points and an integrated fire station. 

The redevelopment is significant for Gikomba because the market has operated for years through densely packed informal structures.

That environment has created challenges for traders and shoppers while making it difficult for emergency services to respond when fires occur. Flooding has also been a recurring problem in the market and surrounding areas. 

The new design is intended to move traders into organised, numbered and ventilated spaces while improving movement through the market.

Fire safety is particularly important.

Gikomba has experienced repeated fires over the years, with some incidents destroying traders' stock and causing deaths. The inclusion of an integrated fire station in the new development is therefore expected to improve emergency response within the market.

The project is also connected to the wider effort to improve the Nairobi River corridor. Earlier clearance of informal structures along the river formed part of the process leading into the redevelopment. 

For thousands of traders, however, redevelopment is ultimately about more than buildings.

Gikomba is a major source of livelihoods, attracting traders and customers from Nairobi and other parts of the country. Any change to the way stalls are allocated, accessed and operated can therefore affect businesses well beyond the market itself.

The first phase now offers a clearer picture of what the transformed market could look like.

As construction continues, attention will turn to completion, allocation of the new trading spaces and how traders will transition into the modernised facility.

For Nairobi, the project represents an attempt to address some of the longstanding problems surrounding one of the city's most important trading hubs while creating a more organised environment for commerce.

articles.title: Nairobi Weather: Cool and Cloudy Conditions Expected This Week
articles.desc: Nairobi is expected to experience intermittent cool and cloudy conditions as Kenya Met forecasts generally dry weather across most of the country.
articles.content:
Nairobi residents can expect intermittent cool and cloudy conditions in the coming days as the Kenya Meteorological Department forecasts generally dry weather across most of Kenya.

The latest seven-day outlook, covering August 13 to 20, places Nairobi among several counties that could experience periods of cloud cover and cooler weather during the forecast period.

The forecast does not place Nairobi among the eight counties specifically highlighted as likely to receive rainfall during the period. Those counties include Bungoma, Trans Nzoia, Nakuru, Uasin Gishu, Elgeyo Marakwet, Kericho, Nyandarua and Nyeri.

For Nairobi residents, the forecast points to weather that may remain noticeably cool and cloudy at intervals rather than a prolonged spell of heavy rain.

That distinction matters for people planning their daily routines.

Commuters, outdoor traders, schools, construction workers and people travelling across the city can use the forecast to prepare for changing conditions, particularly during cooler or overcast periods.

The wider national picture remains relatively dry. Kenya Met expects most parts of the country to experience generally dry conditions, although some areas will continue to receive rainfall.

Nairobi's weather can also change within relatively short periods, meaning residents should not interpret the forecast as a guarantee that every part of the city will experience identical conditions.

The forecast is therefore most useful as a planning guide.

For anyone heading out early, cooler conditions may make warm clothing useful, while motorists and pedestrians should continue paying attention to local conditions where cloud cover or rain develops.

The weather outlook also comes as Kenya continues through the traditionally cool August period, with the Meteorological Department monitoring changing conditions across the country.

For Nairobi, the immediate forecast is less about heavy rainfall and more about cool, cloudy intervals amid generally dry conditions.

Residents should continue monitoring official weather updates as conditions can change and new forecasts are issued.

articles.title: Parklands Demolition Claims Clarified as Nairobi River Work Continues
articles.desc: Nairobi authorities have clarified viral claims about Parklands demolitions as the city continues its programme to restore riparian land along the river.
articles.content:
Viral claims of imminent demolitions in Parklands have prompted clarification from the Nairobi Rivers Commission and the Parks and Recreational Authority as work to reclaim riparian land along Nairobi’s rivers continues.

The clarification follows concerns among residents after information circulated about possible demolitions along the Kibagare River corridor. Officials said residents seeking information about notices, demarcation or verification should use official government channels rather than rely on unverified claims circulating online.

The issue matters because Nairobi’s river restoration programme is increasingly affecting areas where homes, businesses and other developments have been established close to river corridors.

The Nairobi Rivers Commission’s demarcation exercise covers about 27 kilometres, from Gitwamba Bridge to Naivasha Road, with the riparian boundary measured using a 30-metre buffer from the highest water mark, according to the Commission.

For Parklands residents and property owners, the distinction between an official notice, a demarcation exercise and an actual demolition order is important.

Unverified information can quickly create uncertainty for households and businesses, particularly where property ownership, development approvals and environmental regulations intersect.

The wider Nairobi River restoration programme is aimed at reclaiming riparian areas and improving the condition of the city's waterways. The government has been pursuing the programme through a multi-agency approach, with authorities identifying developments considered to be occupying protected river corridors.

That process, however, places a responsibility on authorities to communicate clearly with affected communities.

For residents, knowing whether a property has actually been identified for enforcement action is different from hearing that demolitions are about to take place.

The latest clarification therefore shifts attention back to official verification.
Residents with concerns over specific properties or notices have been urged to seek clarification through the relevant government offices rather than depend on social-media claims.

As Nairobi's river restoration programme continues, the balance between environmental protection, public safety and property interests is likely to remain an important issue for communities located along the city's waterways.

For Parklands, the immediate message is clear: verify before reacting, and seek official information where property or demolition claims are involved.
